description: Test a monitor with a simulated rate change to see if it would trigger. No webhook is sent. It is not a pure dry run: the simulation IS recorded, as a monitor_evaluations row (and a webhook audit row) flagged is_simulation = 1, so it appears in the monitor's history clearly marked as a simulation. It does not touch the monitor's cooldown or last_triggered_at. Use deliver_test_webhook to actually send a test webhook.

monitor_id.description: The unique identifier of the monitor to simulate. Required.

rate_change.description: The simulated rate change event. Required.

product_type.description: The product type that changed (e.g., "30yr_fixed"). Required.

state.description: US state code where the rate changed. Required.

name: simulate_monitor

outputSchema.description: Dry-run evaluation of a monitor against a hypothetical rate change. No webhook is sent and the cooldown is ignored. On a missing id the tool returns a not-found shape instead of throwing.

error.description: Present and set to 'not_found' when the monitor id does not exist.

evaluation.description: Why the monitor did or did not fire.

conditions_met.description: Whether the trigger conditions were satisfied.

rate_change.description: The simulated change, echoed back with rates pre-formatted as percent strings.

change_pct.description: Signed change, formatted as a percent string such as '+0.25%'.

new_rate.description: New rate, formatted as a percent string.

previous_rate.description: Prior rate, formatted as a percent string such as '6.5%'.

product_type.description: Product type of the simulated change.

summary.description: Plain-language verdict on whether the monitor would fire, or a not-found message.

would_trigger.description: Whether the monitor's conditions are satisfied by the supplied change.
